chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Baseer, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: When you intend to leave Mecca, buy dates with a dirham and give them in charity, handful by handful, so that it serves as expiation for whatever was from you during your ihram and whatever was from you in Mecca.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended charity to give when leaving Mecca after Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes this specific charity as a spiritual cleansing for the pilgrim, addressing both the ritual state of *ihram* and the general conduct within Mecca. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on *sunnah* acts that complement obligatory rites, ensuring the pilgrimage is accepted with full spiritual purity. The distribution of dates, a staple of the region, symbolizes humility and the removal of minor spiritual blemishes before returning to daily life.

en.hubeali: Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from the one who mentioned it, from Aban, from Abu Baseer who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘When you want to exit from Makkah, so buy some dates with a Dirham and give in charity with it, a handful, a handful, so it would happen to be (an expiation) for everything what was from you during your being in your Ihraam, and whatever was from you in Makkah’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from those whom he has mentioned from Aban from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When you want to leave Makkah, buy one dirham of dates. Give it as charity, a handful and a handful and it will be (as ransom) for you because of what may have happened during the time you were in the state of Ihram and when you were in Makkah.’” (Fatwa best explains Hadith 2 of this Chapter)
